columnCOverBottomLeft.why: x on c2/c3 and o on a1/b1 each push the unit up and together carry about 73% of its variance; the reading holds, though the two drivers add rather than require each other.

leftXRightO.why: the bottom-row left-against-right pattern carries most of the variance, but per piece o on the upper rows pushes it up as hard as the bottom-row squares, which the reading calls a small push and leaves unexplained.

xRaisedInCentre.why: a default-on unit switched off when x spends its pieces on the bottom row (a1, b1, c1) and kept high by x on the raised central squares, as stated; probes and subgroups confirm both sides.

xOwnsCentreColumn.why: it does fire when x holds d1-d3, but more than half of its active positions have no x in d1-d3, mostly with the centre column still empty.
